extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Art of Computer Programming (TAOCP): mathematicians, computer scientists, advanced students, puzzle solvers, and contributors interested in exercises, errata, and book updates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requests related to checking, reporting, and improving exercises and early (prefascicle) material in The Art of Computer Programming; includes where to report errors and how prefascicles differ from paperback editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit confirmation of exercise correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers are asked to tell Don explicitly: "Dear Don, I have read exercise N and its answer very carefully, and I believe that it is 100% correct," where N is one of the listed exercise numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A long list of specific exercise identifiers is provided (e.g., MPR-28-29, MPR-50, 7.2.2-79, 7.2.2.1-29 and 30, etc.). Send success reports or confirmations to the usual address for bug reports (taocp@cs.stanford.edu). The author welcomes explicit confirmations that an exercise and its answer are 100% correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to peek at answers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Remember that you don't have to work the exercise first. You're allowed to peek at the answer; in fact, you're even encouraged to do so."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance explicitly permits readers to consult answers before attempting exercises, especially when the goal is verification or checking details rather than self-testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward strategy for discovering errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to receive a reward check for discovering an error in TAOCP, the best strategy may well be to scrutinize the answers to the exercises that are listed above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: careful examination of exercise answers (especially those called out) is the appropriate method to find errata worthy of reward; report discoveries via the standard bug-report address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefascicle vs paperback maintenance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefascicles (free preview PostScript files) are 'frozen' and will not be maintained, while the paperback will gradually improve with time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prefascicle contents agree fairly well with the first paperback printing except for parts of the index. Readers should treat prefascicles as static snapshots and expect corrections/improvements in later paperback printings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and difficulty guidance for exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the other exercises (over 750) are 'completely non-scary' and elementary, but some exercises (especially those listed) are 'highly technical' and 'the darker corners of my books are naturally the most difficult to get right.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are reassured that they need not be intimidated; however, the author asks for help checking the finer, high-technicality points. The page enumerates many advanced exercises as suggested targets for careful checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred reporting channel for errata and success reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Send success reports and bug reports to taocp@cs.stanford.edu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the 'usual address for bug reports' and the mechanism by which readers communicate confirmations or discovered errors (and presumably claim any reward checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of modern computational and proof tools in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern methods (state-of-the-art SMT solvers; Lean's Mathlib; frontier LLMs as research agents; and substantial computing power) made recent breakthroughs possible (e.g., solutions up to n = 9 processors and conjectures for larger n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit encouragement that using contemporary automated theorem proving, satisfiability/SMT tooling, formal libraries, and large language models is a valid and productive approach for attacking difficult combinatorial/algorithmic problems arising in TAOCP and related research.
